reason: The only available action is to use the auger on the ice, which seems like the first step toward supplying water to the processor.
expectation: I expect the auger to extract water or ice from the bank, though I don't know what form it will produce.

effect: The well produces untreated water, so the next step is to connect that source for treatment.
reaction: The heated probe producing a cloudy trickle makes the extraction process clearer.
reason: The hose looks useful for carrying water from the well toward the processor, and it is the only combination offered.
expectation: I expect the hose to connect to the well, though it may take another step to reach the processor.

effect: The hose already reaches the processor, and its heated jacket and strainer handle the line and initial grit; treatment and checks still lie ahead.
reaction: The heating jacket and raw-water strainer made the connection more informative than I expected.
reason: The connected line is ready to be used at the processor, and this is the only combination offered.
expectation: I expect the processor to treat the raw water, though drinking-water checks may require another step.

effect: The processor treated and checked the water before opening the tap, completing the potable supply goal.
reaction: The nearly tasteless first cup was a satisfying payoff for the cloudy water from the ice bank.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the well line was most worthwhile: its heated jacket and strainer showed how the raw water reaches the processor and begins to be cleaned.

leastWorthwhile.text: The processor step was predictable because it was the only offered combination, though its explanation of treatment was useful.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the hose connection already included a powered heating jacket and a raw-water strainer.

arbitrary.text: None felt arbitrary; each action had a clear role in extracting, carrying, or treating the water.

continue.text: I would choose to continue because the practical details of making water drinkable were interesting, and I am curious how the expedition develops.
